subject: Deployment mode follow-up: shared vs dedicated isolation & SLOs
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Subject: Deployment mode follow-up: shared vs dedicated isolation & SLOs

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

What we heard:
- Primary workload: real-time text generation for checkout assistants and fraud detection scoring (low-latency, high-throughput bursts).
- Current traffic profile: steady-state with spikes during promotions (you mentioned up to ~800 qps burst).
- Compliance: handling PCI data for payment tokens — data residency and network isolation are important.
- Key concerns: noisy neighbor effects, predictable p95 latency (you mentioned ~200ms target), and clear isolation boundaries for audits.

Options to consider (high-level):
- Hosted API: fastest to go live, cost-effective for early usage, but runs on multi-tenant pools with soft isolation. Not recommended if you need strict PCI isolation or guaranteed SLOs.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for BrightCart — provides strong isolation, predictable throughput, and can be backed by SLA add-ons (we can set committed p95 targets for typical request distributions). Good middle ground for steady production with burst capacity.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed network and full control over infra. Best for strict compliance/regulatory needs (we see this for large PCI/PHI customers).

Noisy-neighbor mitigations we offer (summary):
- Dedicated pools: per-tenant resource reservations and CUDA context isolation to avoid cross-tenant interference.
- QoS controls: per-route rate limits and token-based throttling with graceful degradation policies.
- Autoscaling + burst buffers: configured to absorb transient bursts without impacting p95 for committed capacity.

Attached: SLA_overview.pdf (high-level SLA and SLO options) and network_diagram.png (example VPC flow).

Questions for you before the technical deep-dive so we tailor the PoC:
1) Can you confirm typical steady qps and peak burst qps? (you mentioned ~800 but wanted exact numbers)
2) What p95 latency target do you need for generation endpoints (and at what concurrency)?
3) Is PCI scope limited to token passing (no raw card data stored) or do you need a fully isolated environment for cardholder data?

Next steps:
- If you can share the answers above, Marissa (cc'd) will run a short tech deep-dive and proposal for Dedicated vs Private with capacity sizing.
- Proposed time: Wed 20 Feb, 10:00 AM PT — would that work for your infra/security leads?

Thanks — I’ll wait for the details and will schedule the call once we confirm.

—
Priyom Das

Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: shared vs dedicated isolation & SLOs

Thanks Priyom — great summary. A few answers and clarifications below:

1) Traffic: our normal traffic is ~300 qps for generation endpoints, but we see promotional spikes up to ~900 qps for short windows (~5–10 minutes).
2) Latency target: p95 <= 200ms for the checkout assistant path is our aspirational target; p95 <= 300ms would be acceptable if it’s well documented and rare exceptions are alerted.
3) PCI: we tokenize card numbers at the gateway. We don't store PANs in BrightCart, but our PCI auditor is requesting that any external inference vendor demonstrate network segmentation and clear isolation of systems handling tokens — most likely we’ll ask for evidence during procurement.

Two follow-ups from us:
- Can you share specifics (or a short diagram) on how Dedicated pools prevent noisy-neighbor interference? We need something to show the auditors.
- For a PoC, we’d prefer to try Dedicated (reserved) capacity first — would you be able to support a short-term reserved pool with predictable throughput?

Also looping in our security lead (Olivia) — Olivia, feel free to add anything I missed.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Engineering, BrightCart
samir@brightcart.com

Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: shared vs dedicated isolation & SLOs

Samir — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. Quick answers and next steps below.

Dedicated pool & noisy-neighbor details (for auditors):
- Resource isolation: Dedicated capacity provisions physical GPU nodes (or isolated VMs/nodes in private clusters) that are assigned exclusively to your tenant. We avoid multi-tenant inference on those nodes.
- CUDA/context isolation: each model execution runs in isolated CUDA contexts and we avoid shared persistent state across tenants; KV cache and model weights are memory-isolated per-tenant.
- QoS & rate limiting: per-route/request throttles and leaky-bucket policies to ensure a single tenant cannot saturate shared control-plane resources during public cloud bursts.
- Eviction/fallback: in the rare case of extreme resource pressure, we surface metrics and optionally fail-over to a lower-cost model variant (configurable).

SLOs & sizing:
- Based on your numbers (300 steady / 900 burst), preliminary sizing for Dedicated: 8 reserved GPU units with autoscale headroom to handle short bursts. With that config we can commit to p95 <= 250ms for gen endpoints under normal load and provide an SLA addendum with clearer penalties/credits for missed SLOs. Exact numbers depend on model family, sequence length, and concurrency profile — Marissa will run the sizing exercise.

PCI & evidence:
- I’ll attach a short network diagram and the SLA doc for auditors. For procurement we can provide: architecture diagram, dedicated node commitment statement, and a SOC2 excerpt (or SOC2 letter) — if you need a SOC2 report, let us know and we’ll coordinate with our security team.

PoC: we can stand up a short-term dedicated pool for a 30-day PoC with performance telemetry and a runbook for isolation checks. If the auditor requires, we can gate the PoC behind a Private deployment discussion, but typically Dedicated with proper documentation satisfies the tokenization use-case.

Proposed tech call: Wed, 20 Feb at 10:00 AM PT — Marissa (cc) will lead the infra sizing deep-dive and bring one of our SREs to talk about isolation and the telemetry we expose. Vivek (cc) will join for SLA/contract questions.

Next steps:
- Samir/Olivia: confirm the call time and share any security questionnaire in advance.
- Marissa: I’ll hand off sizing and draft a PoC outline.

—
Priyom
